pages.intro: `MfxClient` signs every request with your Ed25519 key, retries reads within a budget and opens the stream. Build one with `MfxClient.builder(baseUrl, keyId, signingKey)` and close it with try-with-resources. Every call is asynchronous and returns a `CompletableFuture`; a list is also an `Iterable` that follows the cursor.

types.name: Signing
types.doc:
The four headers every MFX Hub request carries, and the exact message their signature covers.

A request is signed, not bearing a token. `X-MFX-Key` names the key. `X-MFX-Timestamp` and `X-MFX-Nonce` make each request usable once. `X-MFX-Signature` is the base64 Ed25519 signature over `timestamp_ms\nnonce\nMETHOD\npath_with_query\nsha256_hex(body)`.

The timestamp is epoch milliseconds and must be within 30 s of the platform's clock. The nonce must be unique per key for five minutes. It is one line of the signed message, so it is restricted to `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{16,64}$`: a nonce with a newline in it could move the line boundaries and sign one request as another. A retry is therefore a new signature, never the same one sent twice.

types.name: MfxJson
types.doc:
How every body is read and written: the API's own field names (the generated models carry them), times as ISO 8601 text, absent fields left out rather than written as null, a field this version does not know yet read past rather than refused, and every `BigDecimal` exact, as a JSON string.

A decimal is a JSON string such as `"1.10450"`, read and written without passing through binary floating point. A JSON number token is refused where a `BigDecimal` is read, because a number has already been through a double in whatever wrote it: `0.07 * 3` is `0.21000000000000002`. The scale is kept, so `"1.10"` goes back out as `"1.10"`, and a decimal is always written plainly, never with an exponent. Text that is not a plain decimal (an exponent, a separator, a space) is refused.

pages.intro: `client.terminals()` provisions, reads, restarts, drains and retires the terminals your key's tenant owns; `client.farms()`, `client.maintenance()` and `client.expertAdvisors()` say where they run, when they pause and which expert advisors they carry.

types.name: Terminals
types.doc:
A tenant's terminals (`client.terminals()`): ask for one, submit the login that makes it real, watch it reach ACTIVE, restart, drain, resume and retire it, and attach an expert advisor to it.

Two rules show up in every signature here. **Every write takes the caller's idempotency key**, with no default: a default would be a value someone did not choose, and the point of the key is that the caller can retry with the same one and get the same answer back rather than a second terminal. And **a credential is a [Secret](#client.Secret)**, not a `String`: it is sent once and never stored, logged or echoed, and printing it shows `***`.

members.name: OPERATION_FINAL
members.doc: An operation is over in any of these; every other state is on its way.

members.name: ON_ITS_WAY
members.doc: The states a terminal passes through on its way to ACTIVE; every other state is settled.

members.name: OFFLINE_IS_TEMPORARY
members.doc: OFFLINE needs nothing from you: the platform brings the terminal back by itself when its host reports again, and moves it to another host of its farm when the host is gone or is still down after fifteen minutes. Retrying a request against an OFFLINE terminal is right; re-creating the terminal is not.

members.name: DEFAULT_WAIT
members.doc: How long the waits wait unless told: fifteen minutes.

members.name: isUsable
members.doc: Can this terminal be used right now: market data, execution, account reads? True only in ACTIVE. Every other state means not yet (REQUESTED, QUEUED, PROVISIONING, LOGGING_IN), not any more (DRAINING, RETIRED), not until it is resumed (DRAINED), or not at the moment (OFFLINE, FAILED). Checking through this means the next state the platform adds cannot quietly read as usable.

members.name: create
members.signature: CompletableFuture<TenantTerminal> create(UUID brokerId, UUID serverId, String idempotencyKey, CreateTerminal options)
members.doc:
Asks for a terminal, answered at once in state `REQUESTED`. The move to a host is asynchronous, and the credential is submitted separately, so a terminal exists before its login does. `instruments` are the broker's own symbol names: MFX never renames an instrument. A farm named in `options` is checked rather than trusted: one that is not yours, or cannot take it, is refused; nothing that fits is `409 no_farm`.

Also callable as `CompletableFuture<TenantTerminal> create(UUID brokerId, UUID serverId, String idempotencyKey)`.

params.name: options
params.doc: the farm, usages, instruments, labels and redundancy

members.name: get
members.doc: One terminal: its state, how long it has been in it, and its observed conditions.

returns.doc: the terminal; fails with [NotFoundException](#errors.NotFoundException) when there is no such terminal or it is another tenant's (never a 403)

members.name: page
members.signature: CompletableFuture<Page<TenantTerminal>> page(@Nullable String cursor, ListTerminals filter)
members.doc:
One page of this tenant's terminals, newest first, retired ones included. Labels and states narrow the list on the platform before the page is cut, so a filtered page is never short for being filtered.

Also callable as `CompletableFuture<Page<TenantTerminal>> page()`.

params.name: cursor
params.doc: the [Page.nextCursor](#client.Page.nextCursor) of the page before; the first page when null

params.name: filter
params.doc: the page size, labels and states to list

returns.doc: the page, with the cursor for the next; no total

members.name: list
members.doc:
Every terminal, following the cursor until it ends, narrowed as [page](#terminals.Terminals.page) is. There is no total and no page number anywhere in the API, so this follows the cursor rather than counting.

Each page is asked for when the one before has been read, one request a page. Iterating blocks on each page's request: run it where blocking is fine, such as a virtual thread. A failure is thrown from `hasNext()` as the [MfxException](#errors.MfxException) it is, not wrapped.

Also callable as `Iterable<TenantTerminal> list()`.

params.name: filter
params.doc: the page size, labels and states to list

returns.doc: every terminal, page by page; each iteration starts again from the first page

members.name: journal
members.doc:
The terminal's MetaTrader journal, newest line first. While the terminal runs the lines are read from its host now (`live`); once it has stopped, failed or been retired they are the last lines its host kept (`last_words`) for 24 hours, and `stopped` says why. A terminal that is not running and holds no last lines is a `409 state_error`; a host that does not answer within 10 s is a `503 upstream_error`.

Also callable as `CompletableFuture<TerminalJournal> journal(UUID terminalId)`.

raises.doc: `lines` is outside 1 to 200, refused here rather than as a 400

members.name: submitCredentials
members.signature: CompletableFuture<CredentialAccepted> submitCredentials(UUID terminalId, long login, Secret password, String server, String idempotencyKey, CredentialSubmission.CredTypeEnum credType)
members.doc:
Puts a broker login on a terminal. An `investor` credential turns execution off, and `execution_disabled` on the answer says so here rather than at the first refused order.

Also callable as `CompletableFuture<CredentialAccepted> submitCredentials(UUID terminalId, long login, Secret password, String server, String idempotencyKey)`.

returns.doc: the reference to the stored credential

members.name: restart
members.signature: CompletableFuture<OperationAccepted> restart(UUID terminalId, String reason, String idempotencyKey, Relaunch options)
members.doc:
Restarts a stuck terminal: the terminal is closed and started again on the same host, answered 202 with the operation to follow. A restart drops the broker session for a few seconds, so on an account with positions open it is refused unless `confirmOpenPositions` says so. `queue` is true unless set: a valid restart refused only because the platform is busy is then answered 202 with the operation `QUEUED`; false keeps the refusal, a 409 or 429 with `Retry-After`.

Also callable as `CompletableFuture<OperationAccepted> restart(UUID terminalId, String reason, String idempotencyKey)`.

params.name: options
params.doc: whether to queue, and whether open positions are confirmed

members.name: replaceInstruments
members.signature: CompletableFuture<TenantTerminal> replaceInstruments(UUID terminalId, List<String> instruments, List<String> depthInstruments, String idempotencyKey)
members.doc:
Replaces the terminal's whole instrument list, and the symbols of it whose order book it reads and streams on [Channel.book](#stream.Channel.book): the whole list, an empty one stopping depth. A farm that offers no depth answers 422 `depth_not_offered`; more than the farm allows, or a symbol not in `instruments`, is 422 `unprocessable`.

Also callable as `CompletableFuture<TenantTerminal> replaceInstruments(UUID terminalId, List<String> instruments, String idempotencyKey)`.

params.name: depthInstruments
params.doc: the symbols of `instruments` to read the book of

members.name: attachExpertAdvisor
members.signature: CompletableFuture<OperationAccepted> attachExpertAdvisor(UUID terminalId, UUID expertAdvisorId, String symbol, ExpertAdvisorAttach.TimeframeEnum timeframe, String reason, String idempotencyKey, Relaunch options)
members.doc:
Attaches an approved version to this terminal, on the symbol's chart and timeframe: a governed relaunch, answered 202 with the operation to follow ([waitForOperation](#terminals.Terminals.waitForOperation)). The expert then runs its trial with trading off; it trades only after a green trial, and on a real-money account only after [confirmExpertAdvisor](#terminals.Terminals.confirmExpertAdvisor). `queue` is false unless set.

Also callable as `CompletableFuture<OperationAccepted> attachExpertAdvisor(UUID terminalId, UUID expertAdvisorId, String symbol, ExpertAdvisorAttach.TimeframeEnum timeframe, String reason, String idempotencyKey)`.

params.name: options
params.doc: whether to queue, and whether open positions are confirmed

members.name: detachExpertAdvisor
members.signature: CompletableFuture<OperationAccepted> detachExpertAdvisor(UUID terminalId, String reason, String idempotencyKey, Relaunch options)
members.doc:
Takes the expert off this terminal: a governed relaunch that rebuilds the folder, answered 202. `queue` is false unless set.

Also callable as `CompletableFuture<OperationAccepted> detachExpertAdvisor(UUID terminalId, String reason, String idempotencyKey)`.

params.name: options
params.doc: whether to queue, and whether open positions are confirmed

members.name: confirmExpertAdvisor
members.doc: Turns on live trading on a real-money account after a green trial, with the one-time code sent to the account's representative. A wrong, used or expired code is 403 `confirmation_refused`, and the answer does not say which; five in a row lock it. The API takes no idempotency key here: the code is good once.

members.name: getOperation
members.doc: One operation on the terminal (restart, attach, detach, drain): its state, step and timeline.

members.name: waitForOperation
members.signature: CompletableFuture<TerminalOperation> waitForOperation(UUID terminalId, UUID operationId, Duration timeout)
members.doc:
Reads the operation until it is over ([OPERATION_FINAL](#terminals.Terminals.OPERATION_FINAL)), or until `timeout` has passed on the client's clock, waiting 2 s, then doubling to 15 s, between reads. Completes with the last read either way: an operation still running when the time runs out is reported as it is. Serves restart, attach, detach and drain alike.

Also callable as `CompletableFuture<TerminalOperation> waitForOperation(UUID terminalId, UUID operationId)`.

members.name: waitUntilActive
members.doc:
Reads the terminal until it is no longer on its way to ACTIVE ([ON_ITS_WAY](#terminals.Terminals.ON_ITS_WAY)), or until `timeout` has been waited. Completes with the last read either way: ACTIVE, a state it settled in instead (FAILED, for one), or still on its way when the time ran out. A QUEUED terminal is read again at its `queue.expected_start_at` (between 2 s and a minute away), not on a fixed beat; any other state is read again after 2 s, doubling to 15 s.

Also callable as `CompletableFuture<TenantTerminal> waitUntilActive(UUID terminalId)`.

params.name: timeout
params.doc: how long to wait in all; zero reads once

raises.doc: the timeout is below zero

members.name: bulkRestart
members.signature: CompletableFuture<BulkAction> bulkRestart(String reason, String idempotencyKey, BulkRestart which)
members.doc: Restarts many of your terminals at once: those on a farm, at a broker, or listed (at most 1000), and at least one of the three. Each is judged by the rules of a single restart; a refused one is listed in `refused` with its rule's code, and the rest are taken. Without `confirmOpenPositions` a terminal with positions open is refused (`positions_open`) and the rest go ahead.

params.name: reason
params.doc: 1 to 500 characters, for the audit log

params.name: which
params.doc: the farm, broker or terminals, and whether open positions are confirmed

returns.doc: the action, with its expected finish

raises.doc: the reason is blank or too long, nothing is named, or more than 1000 terminals are; checked here so a bad one is ours, not a 422

members.name: getBulkAction
members.doc: A bulk action's progress: counts per state, what was refused, and its expected finish.

members.name: cancelBulkAction
members.doc: Cancels a bulk action: its items still QUEUED settle CANCELLED, running ones finish.

members.name: drain
members.signature: CompletableFuture<TenantTerminal> drain(UUID terminalId, String idempotencyKey, DrainTerminal options)
members.doc:
Closes the terminal gracefully and keeps it: DRAINED holds no host and is not billed. Answered with the terminal `DRAINING`; it is `DRAINED` once its host has stopped it. A drained terminal keeps its id, account, credential, instruments, labels and expert-advisor record and runs nothing until [resume](#terminals.Terminals.resume); it still counts toward the terminal quota. Governed as a restart is; `confirmOpenPositions` is required when the account has positions open (409 `positions_open`).

Also callable as `CompletableFuture<TenantTerminal> drain(UUID terminalId, String idempotencyKey)`.

params.name: options
params.doc: the reason for the audit log, and whether open positions are confirmed

members.name: resume
members.doc: Places a DRAINED terminal again: back to `REQUESTED`, then placed and logged in as new. What can never work is refused at once; a terminal already on its way back is answered as it is, so a resume sent twice is one resume; a DRAINING one is 409 `state_error` until it is DRAINED.

members.name: retire
members.doc: Retires a terminal: it drains, then retires.

returns.doc: the terminal as it is now, DRAINING

types.name: Execution
types.doc:
Placing and changing orders (`client.execution()` on a terminal; the same commands on a trading account through `client.tradingAccounts()`).

Every method completes with an [ExecutionResult](#execution.ExecutionResult) and **never completes exceptionally**. A transport fault, a timeout, a rate limit, a refusal and a broker rejection are all outcomes of trying to trade, and a caller that must catch each one to learn whether it has a position will eventually place two. Execution is asynchronous by design: the platform answers 202 with a command id once the command is persisted, and the outcome arrives later on the stream or from [getCommand](#execution.Execution.getCommand); [waitFor](#execution.Execution.waitFor) polls until it is final.

Three rules show up in every signature. **The idempotency key is the caller's**: a retry reuses it and gets the original command back with `duplicate` true, never a second order. **Nothing is retried automatically**: not a timeout, not a rate limit, not a 5xx. And **a decimal is a `BigDecimal`**, never a double, written plainly (`1E+3` goes as `"1000"`). Malformed arguments (a negative volume, a blank key) are refused before anything is sent, by throwing.

members.doc: The longest comment the terminal keeps whole, in characters (the contract's `maxLength`).

types.name: ExecutionResult
types.signature: record ExecutionResult(boolean ok, String idempotencyKey, double clientRttMs, @Nullable UUID commandId, @Nullable CommandState state, boolean isFinal, boolean retryable, boolean duplicate, @Nullable Reason reason, @Nullable String reasonText, @Nullable Integer mt5Retcode, @Nullable String retcodeText, @Nullable String commentRaw, @Nullable String terminalState, Tickets tickets, @Nullable BigDecimal execPrice, @Nullable BigDecimal execVolume, @Nullable Integer brokerLatencyMs, @Nullable Integer agentLatencyMs, int attempts, @Nullable String reroutedFrom, @Nullable String detail, @Nullable OffsetDateTime retryAt, @Nullable String venue, @Nullable String venueCode, List<VenueDeal> deals, @Nullable BigDecimal volumeUnits, boolean closeByEmulated, boolean protectionNotSet)

The whole answer to one execution call. Never thrown: always the value the future completes with.

**Execution never fails across this boundary.** A transport fault, a timeout, a rate limit and a broker rejection are all results, because a trading loop that has to catch exceptions to find out whether it has a position is a trading loop that will one day place two.

Read [state](#execution.ExecutionResult.state) first: SUCCEEDED is done; FAILED, EXPIRED and REJECTED did not happen; UNKNOWN may already be a position and must never be sent again under a new key. [isFinal](#execution.ExecutionResult.isFinal) says whether the platform can still change the answer; [Execution.waitFor](#execution.Execution.waitFor) waits until it cannot. [retryable](#execution.ExecutionResult.retryable) is false while a command is UNKNOWN, and it is the flag to act on.

types.doc: What a terminal's account looks like right now (`client.accounts()`): reads, failing with the typed errors. Live lists are snapshots: positions and pending orders come back whole with their `as_of`, never behind a cursor. History (deals) is paged, newest first, inside a window. Everything carries when it was observed, and a half never observed is null rather than zero.

members.name: positions

members.signature: CompletableFuture<Page<Deal>> deals(UUID terminalId, OffsetDateTime from, OffsetDateTime to, @Nullable String cursor, @Nullable Integer limit)

Closed deals, newest first, inside a window. The window is required, by the API and so by this: an unbounded history request over a partitioned table is the query that takes a database down.

Reads fail with the typed errors; nothing here is an execution call.

members.doc:
One page of the brokers MFX supports, with each one's status: `active` is usable, `suspended` and `retired` are not. A terminal requested on a broker that is not usable is refused with [UnsupportedBrokerException](#errors.UnsupportedBrokerException).

A terminal on a disabled server is refused as [UnsupportedBrokerException](#errors.UnsupportedBrokerException) naming `server_disabled`: try another server of this broker. One page.

Also callable as `CompletableFuture<Page<TenantBrokerServer>> servers(UUID brokerId)`.

A broker you hold no catalogue for answers an empty list.

The page's [Page.source](#client.Page.source) is `live` when a terminal of yours runs on the server and account type, `last_known` when none does any more.

members.signature: CompletableFuture<SymbolQuote> quote(UUID brokerId, String symbol, WhichServer which)
members.doc:
The current quote for one symbol, with its age: a quote is never returned without saying how old it is, because a stale quote reads exactly like a live one and gets acted on. members.name: candles
members.signature: CompletableFuture<CandleList> candles(UUID broker, String symbol, Timeframe timeframe, OffsetDateTime from, OffsetDateTime to, @Nullable Integer limit, @Nullable UUID serverId)
members.doc:
A symbol's bars for a window, oldest first, at most 1,000 a call: the ones the broker's server shows the tenant's own account, read through one of its ACTIVE terminals there. When the window holds more than `limit` bars the answer is the newest of them; ask again with an earlier `to` for the ones before. The bar still forming is included when the window reaches it. Each bar's `ts` is its open time as a true instant. No bar in the window is an empty answer, not an error.

Also callable as `CompletableFuture<CandleList> candles(UUID broker, String symbol, Timeframe timeframe, OffsetDateTime from, OffsetDateTime to)`.

When the window holds more than `limit` bars the answer is the newest of them. Each read counts against the same per-terminal limit as [candles](#market-data.MarketData.candles). A MetaTrader account is a [StateException](#errors.StateException) (`not_on_this_venue`); an account whose runner is not connected is an [UpstreamException](#errors.UpstreamException).

Also callable as `CompletableFuture<CandleList> accountCandles(UUID accountId, String symbol, Timeframe timeframe, OffsetDateTime from, OffsetDateTime to)`.

params.name: symbol
params.doc: the account's own name for it

params.name: limit

One read of tick history: the first `limit` ticks at or after `from`, oldest first, read through one of the tenant's ACTIVE terminals on the broker's server. MFX keeps no tick store of its own, so how far back they go is the broker's to say. `more` on the answer is true when the window holds ticks beyond the ones returned: [allTicks](#market-data.MarketData.allTicks) follows it.

Also callable as `CompletableFuture<TickList> ticks(UUID broker, String symbol, OffsetDateTime from)`.

params.doc: leaves out ticks after it; none when null

params.name: limit
params.doc: at most this many (1,000 by default)

The contract's way to continue is to ask again from the last tick's time, and several ticks can share one millisecond, so the next answer begins with ticks already held: this drops exactly those and yields the rest. pages.intro: `client.stream()` opens one WebSocket for many channels, resumable by sequence number across reconnects. `MfxStream` is an `Iterable` of `StreamEvent`; `Events.eventOf` reads a message as its typed event, and `LiveAccount` keeps an account's view current from it.

types.name: MfxStream
types.signature: final class MfxStream implements AutoCloseable, Iterable<StreamEvent>
types.doc:
The multiplexed stream: ticks, candles, events and results on one signed WebSocket.

A reconnect resumes what can be resumed and counts the rest: events, results, account and expert channels carry a per-channel `seq` and are resumed from the last one seen; ticks and candles subscribe again, and their gap is counted rather than hidden.

Nothing is buffered on the caller's behalf: a read takes the next frame from the socket, so a slow consumer meets real backpressure and is closed by the platform with 4008, which is counted. Close code 4001 (re-authenticate) fails the read with [AuthException](#errors.AuthException): every reconnect would meet the same wall, and a client spinning on a revoked key looks like an outage.

Read it with [next](#stream.MfxStream.next), or iterate it, which blocks on each event; close it with [close](#stream.MfxStream.close), or try-with-resources.

types.name: Risk
types.doc:
Risk Management (`client.risk()`): policies and their versions, the accounts they protect and their figures, the planner, exit plans, challenges and the activity. `risk:read` to read, `risk:write` to change, `risk:override` to relax protection or clear a breach; every route needs Risk Management in the plan.

Rules, resets, orders, steps and requests are given in the API's own names, as a `Map` (or the generated model where a method takes one). A figure in them is a `BigDecimal`, written as exact text, or a string; a `double` anywhere is refused before anything is sent. Every write takes the caller's idempotency key and is never retried.

pages.intro: `client.copy()` runs copy trading: leaders, followers and their mandates, groups, signals, and what each copy did.

types.name: Copy
types.doc:
Copy Trading for this key's tenant (`client.copy()`; `copy:read` and `copy:write`): leaders, followers, groups, stop-outs, requested closes, the leaders' signals and the copy log.

Every write takes the caller's idempotency key and is never retried. Nested settings are maps in the contract's own names; each body is checked against the contract before anything is sent, so a name the contract does not have, a value it cannot hold, or a double anywhere is an `IllegalArgumentException` at the call. Every list page carries its `stats` row.

types.name: BillingPaymentRequiredException
types.doc:
402 `billing_payment_required`: a payment is missing on the billing profile the request falls under, and nothing was done.

It is **not retryable**: sending the same request again changes nothing until the payment is made. At `stage` `reminder` it comes only from a request that adds something billed. Once `stage` is `suspended` it can come from **any write** on the tenant or the profile, whatever route it was sent to. **Reads keep working** throughout, the billing reads included.

What a caller does: show `getMessage` and [action](#errors.BillingPaymentRequiredException.action) to a person; once paid, send the request again (a write under the same idempotency key). Execution never fails: an order refused for billing completes as a refused [ExecutionResult](#execution.ExecutionResult) whose `detail` carries this error's text. The cause of the standing is [billingCause](#errors.BillingPaymentRequiredException.billingCause), never `getCause()`, which is the Java exception's own.

types.name: TermsNotAcceptedException

types.name: ServiceAgreementNotAcceptedException
types.doc:
409 `service_agreement_not_accepted`: the organisation is moving to another plan and the new plan's Service Agreement is not accepted yet, or a version of its plan's Service Agreement that must be accepted is past its grace period unaccepted. Until it is accepted, adding a terminal, attaching an expert advisor, generating or replacing an API key and asking for higher limits are refused.

It is **not retryable** unchanged. **Nothing running is touched**: every read, order and position call works. What a caller does: show `getMessage` and [acceptUrl](#errors.ServiceAgreementNotAcceptedException.acceptUrl) to an owner or admin of the organisation, who accepts in the customer portal; then send the request again. `client.tenant().serviceAgreement()` says what is due. Where the Terms are held as well, this error answers and [documents](#errors.ServiceAgreementNotAcceptedException.documents) lists every document due.
